concerns.text: Phase 9 (T090–T094) introduces 'Rule Space Enumeration' to 'mine the computational universe' and find the 'simplest universal rule.' This violates Constitution Principle VI (Biological Constraint Fidelity) which mandates strict adherence to the specified laminar structure, and contradicts the Spec (US-003) which limits scope to ablation of a *parameterized* microcircuit. This is a semantic weakening of the research constraint by replacing a specific biological hypothesis with an unbounded search.

Task T014 (implement `validate_generalization` and produce `generalization_report.md`) is marked as missing/invalid in the provided text context (implied by 'REJECTED' status in prior analysis). Without this task, FR-006 (validate on independent test set) and US-001 Acceptance Scenario 2 (demonstrate <10% degradation on independent set) have no implementation path. The deliverable for FR-006 is dropped.

Success Criterion SC-002 requires measuring training stability (gradient norms) against the baseline. T010b (log gradient norms) and T071 (verify distribution) are present but T011b (integration test asserting file existence and validity) is marked as optional/missing in the text. Without a blocking test asserting the artifact `data/logs/gradient_norms.json` exists and is valid, SC-002 is untestable and effectively dropped.

Task T085 asserts 'physically plausible bounds' for the scaling exponent (e.g., beta between -1 and 0) without a basis in the Spec or Plan. The Spec (US-003) only requires reporting the exponent and determining if it is linear/sublinear/superlinear. Imposing arbitrary physical bounds not defined in the requirements constitutes a silent narrowing of the acceptance criteria and introduces a potential false-negative constraint.
